## Observed (pm 2026.10.15; also on 2026.10.14)

A dependency row with only `id` and `kind` (no `created_at`) makes `pm get` crash with an unhandled TypeError:

```console
$ pm update rp-xhnl --dep "id=rp-138k,kind=blocks" --dep "id=rp-ono1,kind=related"
# then the dependency table in tasks/rp-xhnl.toon is reduced to
#   dependencies[2]{id,kind}:
#     rp-138k,blocks
#     rp-ono1,related
$ pm get rp-xhnl
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')
$ pm list --limit 5     # still works
$ pm validate           # no check flags the malformed dependency rows
```

Supplying `created_at` on each dependency makes the item readable again. A single dependency row without `created_at` does not crash; two or more do. That suggests the dependency sort compares `created_at` with `localeCompare` without guarding against `undefined`.

## How agents hit this

Dependency rows written by imports, by hand-edited `.toon` files, by other implementations of the format, or by older tools can lack `created_at`. pm-rust's differential suite hit it with fixture items, and pm-rust now has to keep timestamps in every fixture row to work around it. For an agent, the failure is opaque: no item id, no field name, no recovery hint, and `pm validate` reports nothing.

## Expected

- Reading an item never crashes on a missing optional dependency field. Sort with a stable fallback, for example by `created_at` when present, then `kind`, then `id`.
- Or, if `created_at` is meant to be required, `pm validate` / `pm health` names the item and dependency rows. Reads then fail with a typed, actionable error that has a recovery command, not a TypeError.
GH-1482: pm get crashes with TypeError (localeCompare) when two or more dependency rows lack created_at, and pm validate does not flag them

GitHub report https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1482. Reading multiple dependency rows missing timestamps yields a stable safe result or a typed actionable diagnostic, and validation exposes malformed required data.

Two or more dependency rows without created_at never produce an unhandled TypeError; Ordering or typed refusal is deterministic and documents recovery; Validation and health expose required-field defects where appropriate
Reading multiple dependency rows missing timestamps yields a stable safe result or a typed actionable diagnostic, and validation exposes malformed required data.
